entry.title: Access status rechecked 16 Oct 2026, 05:21 UTC: signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price unchanged. TypeSafe released Jev 1.14 under jev-preview (jev-latest still on jev-1.13.0, moving in about a week per TypeSafe); its models page no longer lists rate-limit numbers (set per organization, shown in the console); image input, a Box question type and 262k long context are opt-in experiments. Home shows four notices; the hidden Series A notice retired at the end of its seven-day shelf life.

When Jev fails: the last 11 bypass cells (judge tools 4, frameworks 3, browser agents 3, email 1) and the last malformed cell were read at their pinned commits. Every failure cell (no key, error, malformed answer, below threshold, bypass) is now recorded for all 77 implementations. Bypass recorded for 77 of 77; 13 are "none found". Malformed answer: 35 fail closed, 24 fall back, 11 fail open, 4 no decision, 3 advisory. Seven existing cell texts were corrected without changing their terms.

Model IDs and aliases: TypeSafe released Jev 1.14 (jev-1.14.0) under jev-preview on 14 Oct; jev-latest still points to jev-1.13.0, and TypeSafe says it moves in about a week. OpenRouter, Vercel and Netlify list 1.14; Cloudflare, Opper, Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry did not list it on 16 Oct. Image input, a Box question type and 262k long context are opt-in experiments that TypeSafe calls not production-ready. The page is retitled "Jev 1.14 preview, 1.13 and jev-latest (TypeSafe AI): model IDs and aliases by route"; its URL is unchanged.

Limitations: "Is Jev multimodal?" now reads: text by default, with image input as an opt-in experiment since 14 Oct that TypeSafe calls not production-ready; no audio or video. The rate-limit row notes that the models page no longer lists numbers.

Decisions API vs Jev vs Microsoft Decision 1: Jev's Images cell is now "text by default; images experimental behind an opt-in header"; its limits cell notes that rate limits are set per organization and no longer published. The copy block and the changed-since list are updated. Prices in all four columns are unchanged (checked 16 Oct).

Claude Code and MCP guardrails: versions rechecked on 16 Oct (oh-my-claudecode 5.7.3: Jev hook files unchanged), and no failure path changed. 32 further projects seen in scans are classified in a lead table: 16 hooks or plugins, 12 that return Jev's answer to the agent, 1 skill, 3 not Jev. The page has a new title; its URL is unchanged.

Build: typesafe-sdk 0.7.5 and @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.7.0 (14 Oct) and @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai 3.0.20 (15 Oct) add image support for the Jev 1.14 preview. Their failure paths were last read at 0.7.4, 0.6.0 and 3.0.18. pydantic-ai-slim 2.57.0 rejects image requests before any call, and DeepEval 4.3.0 leaves its JevEval files unchanged.

Benchmarks: the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v1.0 (13 Oct; Jev 1.13 58, GLiDE 54, Microsoft-Decision-1 54) is listed as a Reported third-party index. It is outside the graded ledger, which stays at 41 rows; one of its four evaluations uses private questions, and it does not state the model ID or route.
Research report of 16 October 2026: bypass cells complete, the Jev 1.14 preview and Claude Code guardrails rechecked. It covers what was read, what changed and what is still not verified.

Access status rechecked 14 Oct 2026, 16:46 UTC: unchanged (signups open, no new-user credit, API operational). Price, listed limits, model aliases and the model IDs on all six routes unchanged; API 90-day uptime 99.837% (99.838% on 13 Oct) with no new status-page event; the status page now also lists two regional API entries, us-east-1 and us-east-2. Two notices shown as on 13 Oct; the hidden notice on TypeSafe's Jack & Jill case study retired at the end of its seven-day shelf life (the case study stays a vendor lead on benchmarks).

When Jev fails: no-key, bypass and n8n below-threshold cells settled for ticket triage, email and lead sorting, n8n, browser and computer use and three single rows, read at the published pins. No key: 50 fail closed, 17 fall back, 7 fail open, 3 advisory, 0 not recorded (8 before). Bypass recorded for 66 of 77 (52 before); 11 not recorded: judge tools 4, frameworks 3, browser agents 3, email 1. A bypass cell counts as recorded only when every entry point was read.

n8n: without a credential, each of the 5 Jev nodes stops with n8n's 'Node does not have any credentials set' error when Continue On Fail is off (n8n release 2.44.1); with it on, the item goes to an error or review output, carries an error field, or passes through unchanged, depending on the node.

Python: typesafe-sdk 0.7.4 (released 9 Oct) keeps a 10 s timeout and 2 retries on 408, 429 and 5xx within 30 s; a missing key raises TypeSafeError when the client is created. Example pins moved to 0.7.4; older version notes collected in one dated list. New title: Jev Python SDK (TypeSafe AI).

TypeScript: ai 7.0.140 renamed experimental_evaluate to experimental_decide (the old name still works as a deprecated alias); with @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai 3.0.18 a missing key throws LoadAPIKeyError at the first call; @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 throws at client creation. One version block and a dated list of earlier checks.

Benchmarks: B44 graded A (48-game Tetris round robin: Microsoft-Decision-1 won 15, Jev 12, OpenAI's Decisions API 11, Laya 8, 2 draws) and B43 graded B (SubQ Snap and Jev level on SWE-bench Verified file localization; the operator takes part in Subquadratic's prize challenge). 41 graded rows (A 12, B 14, C 8, D 7).

Alternatives: SubQ Snap (Subquadratic) added as a hosted decision API with Jev's request shape, $0.05 per 1M input tokens, in public preview; its Terms and its data-retention docs give different retention (both quoted). 34 substitutes; hosted APIs from other providers 4.

Decisions API vs Jev vs Microsoft Decision 1: B44 (grade A, Tetris round robin) added to the graded-tests row and the copyable summary; no price or status cell changed (checked 14 Oct 2026, 16:48 UTC); the SubQ Snap line now links its row on Jev alternatives.
Research report of 14 October 2026: what implementations do with no key, code paths that skip Jev, the Python and TypeScript SDK refresh, B43 and B44, SubQ Snap, and the access recheck.

Evidence notes from 9 October 2026 on Jev rerankers and SQL and document projects reorganised as a topic page: tables of what each implementation does on a Jev error and with no key, the 9 Oct access snapshot, version checks and open questions, with the statements that lack a surviving source link marked. The 9 Oct failure count now points to the current When Jev fails page. Links from the research index, the reranking, SQL and failure pages and the access pages now use the new title.

New page: Jev reranking and document pipelines, evidence notes dated 9 Oct 2026. What five Jev rerankers and context filters and five SQL and document projects did when the Jev call failed, as read in source that day; six more SQL extensions that call Jev (failure paths not read); the 9 Oct access and price snapshot, version checks and OpenRouter route metadata; open questions about jev-approvals, openlayer jevals, pg-redact and rh-guard. Dated observations, not rechecked since.
